$$
f_x(x,y)=2x+y.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The plane $y=-1$ holds $y$ fixed, so $x$ varies and the slope in this slice is $f_x(2,-1)$:

$$
m=f_x(2,-1)=2(2)+(-1)=3.
$$

A change of $1$ in $x$ along the tangent gives a change of $3$ in $z$, with no change in $y$. Hence $\langle 1,0,3\rangle$ is a tangent vector.

Using the point-slope equation, the tangent line through $P(2,-1,3)$ is the intersection

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y&=-1 \\ z-3&=3(x-2)\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The second plane can be written $3x-z-3=0$. Its normal is $\mathbf n_2=\langle 3,0,-1\rangle$, while a normal to $y=-1$ is $\mathbf n_1=\langle 0,1,0\rangle$. Thus

$$
\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2
=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k \\ 0&1&0 \\ 3&0&-1\end{vmatrix}
=\langle -1,0,-3\rangle.
$$

Its negative is the listed vector $\langle 1,0,3\rangle$. The component ratio is $v_z/v_x=3$; $\langle 3,0,1\rangle$ would instead give slope $1/3$.

=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k \\ 1&0&0 \\ 0&1&\sqrt{3}\end{vmatrix}
=\langle 0,-\sqrt{3},1\rangle.
$$

Both signs of a direction vector are allowed, but the component ratio must be preserved. For example, $\langle 0,-1,\sqrt{3}\rangle$ has slope $-\sqrt{3}$, so it is not parallel to this tangent.

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\text{d}s=\int_a^b f(r(t))\,\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t)$ and $\|r^{\prime}(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t \sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 2 \sin{\left(t \right)})j \\ &=(2)(-\sin t+\sin t+t\cos t)i+(2)(\cos t-\cos t+t\sin t)j \\ &=(2 t \cos{\left(t \right)})i+(2 t \sin{\left(t \right)})j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(2 t \cos{\left(t \right)})^2+(2 t \sin{\left(t \right)})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{4t^2(\cos^2t+\sin^2t)} \\ &=2|t| \\ &=2 t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $|t|=t$ since $t\geq0$ along the path of $C.$
